description: The provided image displays two separate bar charts, both plotting Fleiss Kappa values against different axes. The left chart has a vertical y-axis labeled “Fleiss Kappa,” scaled linearly from 0.0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, and a horizontal x-axis labeled “Ambiguity Std,” which appears to represent standard deviation values (0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94). The chart contains four vertical bars, all colored blue, with their values explicitly labeled above them: the first bar at x=0.0 reaches 0.88, the second at x=0.47 reaches 0.46, the third at x=0.82 reaches 0.03, and the fourth at x=0.94 reaches 0.24. The right chart also has a vertical y-axis labeled “Fleiss Kappa,” scaled linearly from 0.0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, and a horizontal x-axis labeled “Max Ambiguity,” which is numerically scaled from 1 to 3. This chart contains three vertical bars, all colored blue, with their values explicitly labeled above them: the bar at x=1 reaches 0.89, the bar at x=2 reaches 0.46, and the bar at x=3 reaches 0.23. Both charts present Fleiss Kappa scores as a measure of inter-rater agreement, with the bars visually indicating the score for each specified level of ambiguity.
